waveName: Wave 4 – Cut placement & accents, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detection

package.title: Instant progress counts, no stats storms, progress carried over on recompute, progress in project lists
package.goal: A laying tap costs microseconds instead of a full grid rescan. Background statistics never pile up. Recomputing with an unchanged layout keeps laid stones that are provably identical. Project lists show the percentage laid. Pinned colours reach the compute.
steps:
progressIndex.ts:
- buildProgressIndex(layout, data, sections) in one pass: secOfRow, secOfCol, placed[], total[], plus a copy of the masks. It uses cellPieceCount only.
- applyDirty(index, data, dirtyCells): popcount difference against the stored mask, then update it.
Rebuild the index on computed, sections or version change. touchProgress(dirtyCells) applies the deltas, or rebuilds when no cells are given. The progress memo reads the index.

Stats: remove progressVersion from the stats effect deps. Keep one stats job in flight; while it runs, a new request only sets a dirty flag, and one more job runs when the current one returns. When the inputs change, cancel an outdated running job with cancelChannel('stats') and ignore the 'abgebrochen' rejection.

db.ts: add meta.progressSummary {placed, total}. Write it with every progress save and clear it on recompute. Projects.tsx and the Home recent cards show 'NN % verlegt' with a mini ProgressBar only when the field exists.
compute params: pass pinnedColors from rec.settings.pinnedColors, converted to FixedColor (lab from hex).
acceptance: Vitest: after random toggles, setCellPlaced, setRangePlaced and kind/colour edits, the index equals progressOf per section and in total.
Carry-over: recomputing with identical settings keeps 100 % of laid stones. A joint change keeps 0 and reports it. A piece whose colour changed is reset and listed.

e2e: 12 laying taps 2 s apart on a project of about 1.4M stones post at most 2 stats worker messages (counted via an init script) and no tap long task over 50 ms on desktop. After marking a section, 'Meine Projekte' shows the percentage.
package.risk: Effort M-L. Never carry over a laid bit unless it is proven identical (requirement 18). Old projects simply show no percentage until they are opened.

findings.title: Each laying-mode tap rescans the whole grid on the main thread and starts a full stats recompute in the worker
findings.problem: Marking a stone as laid only flips one bit. But touchProgress bumps progressVersion, which (a) re-runs the progress useMemo: progressOf over all cells for the total and again over every section (useProject.ts:222 to 228), and (b) restarts the stats effect, which has progressVersion in its dependencies (useProject.ts:272). That repacks the whole mosaic, clones it to the worker and recomputes all geometry stats only to update the 'placed' columns. The worker is single-threaded, so a real edit made shortly after a tap waits behind this run.
findings.evidence: Main-thread CPU profile of 5 taps on the 2M project (browser-prof-tap.cjs, browser/prof2m/taps.cpuprofile): the bundle functions Ar, jr and kr, identified as progressOf, pieceCountFast and popcount via identify-fn.cjs, take 111 ms of about 140 ms of non-idle JS. 5M desktop: one long task per tap of 62, 63, 82, 59 and 54 ms (browser/b5m/result.json tap5_longTasks). Each tap batch then starts a stats worker run of 2,374 ms at 2M with 24.7 ms of main-thread postMessage clone (browser/b2m tap5_worker), and about 6 s at 5M. Mobile emulation (412x915, CDP CPU 4x) on only 55k positions: long tasks of 115, 73, 82, 67 and 65 ms per tap (browser/m55k/result.json). All paths are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/performance-scale/.
findings.proposal: Keep progress counters incrementally. After compute or load, build Int32Array placedPerSection, totalPerSection and placedPerSectionColor in one pass (a few ms with typed arrays). togglePiecePlaced updates them in O(1): look up the section with sectionOfCell and the color with cellPieces(...)[piece].color. setRangePlaced recounts only that section. The progress useMemo reads these counters. Remove progressVersion from the stats effect dependencies, and take ColorStat.placed and Stats.placed from the counters. Optionally send only {idx, mask} diffs to a stats worker that keeps the mosaic in memory.
corrected:
1. Counters in useProject.ts. Keep a ref holding secTotal and secPlaced (Int32Array indexed by section index) plus grand totals.
   - Rebuild them in ONE pass over sections.sections, using cellPieceCount and a popcount of the progress mask, whenever computed, sections or version change. That covers load, compute and every mosaic edit, because setCellKind and setFreePieces reset progress and setPieceColor moves stones between colors.
   - Measured cost is about 30 ms at 5.5M cells, compared with about 60 ms on every tap today.
   - The progress useMemo (useProject.ts:222-228) should just read these counters when progressVersion changes, with no grid scan.

2. One entry point for progress changes. Add api.setPieceMask(idx, newMask), with toggle, cell and range helpers on top of it.
   - It reads oldMask, writes data.progress[idx], and finds the section with sectionOfCell (a binary search).
   - It adds popcount(new & full) - popcount(old & full) to secPlaced[s] and to the grand total, then calls touchProgress.
   - The range helper replaces setRangePlaced and recounts only that section.
   - Route ALL four call sites through it: StepPlan.tsx:100 (lay-mode tap), StepPlan.tsx:210 and 220 (section buttons), StoneDialog.tsx:161 (togglePiecePlaced) and StoneDialog.tsx:172 (setCellPlaced).

3. Stats worker. Remove progressVersion from the dependencies at useProject.ts:272. The only UI consumer of worker-computed placed counts is SectionLegend (StepPlan.tsx:272-291) for the selected section.
   - Compute its per-color placed counts on demand in a useMemo keyed on the selected section, version and progressVersion. Loop over that section's cells only and look up colors without geometry: c1 for FULL, c1/c2 for DIAG and LINE, sub[i] for SUB, free[i].color for FREE. Skip colors outside the palette, as computeStats does.
   - Render these counts instead of c.placed and st.placed. A section is a few tens of thousands of cells, well under 1 ms.
   - PDF and CSV keep computing progress fresh in their own workers, so they are unaffected.

4. Stale stats runs. When the stats effect fires while an earlier stats request is still pending, call cancelChannel('stats') first. A real edit then never waits behind a stale multi-second run (about 2.4 s at 2M and about 6 s at 5M in the auditor's data).

5. Tests (vitest). After random toggles, setCellPlaced, setRangePlaced and kind or color edits, check that:
   - the counters equal progressOf, both per section and in total;
   - the on-demand per-color counts equal computeStats(...).perColor[].placed for that section.
   This keeps the displayed numbers exact, as requirement 18 demands.

6. Scope note. This fixes tap latency for projects with 1M+ positions. It does NOT fix the 60-90 ms tap long tasks on phones for small projects (55k positions, CPU 4x). There progressOf is only about 5 ms per tap, and the cost is the full Viewer redraw on every progressVersion change (Viewer.tsx:144: renderMosaic plus getComputedStyle on each draw) and paint. That needs a separate change: on progress-only changes, repaint just the tapped cell's screen rectangle, or cache the --viewer-bg value.

Effort S-M. Every number shown stays derived from data.progress and data.kind and is never estimated.

1) Stop the stats storm. Remove progressVersion from the stats effect deps (useProject.ts:272). Delete Stats.placed and ColorStat.placed from stats.ts:161-178 so a stale snapshot can never be displayed. For SectionLegend (StepPlan.tsx:270-293), compute per-color placed on the main thread:
- Use a useMemo keyed on [sec, api.version, api.progressVersion].
- Loop only over that section's cells (r0..r1, c0..c1) with a new pure helper in pieces.ts, pieceColor(data, idx, i). It must follow the same piece order as cellPieces: FULL gives c1; DIAG_A, DIAG_B and LINE give c1 then c2; SUB gives sub[i]; FREE gives free[i].color.
- Count bit i of progress[idx] for i < cellPieceCount.
- A 300x300 mm section is at most about 15k cells, which takes under 1 ms.

2) Coalesce stats jobs (useProject.ts:247-272). Keep at most one stats job in flight. If a new request arrives while one is running, only set a dirty flag. When the running job resolves, post exactly one new job if the flag is set. This bounds the worker queue and the cloned-mosaic memory to one copy, and stops real edits from waiting behind obsolete jobs. Measured today without this: 18.7 s latency after 12 taps on 3.1M.

3) Progress counters in a new pure module, src/core/progressIndex.ts:
- buildProgressIndex(layout, data, sections) makes one pass over all cells. It returns {secOfRow: Int32Array, secOfCol: Int32Array, placed: Int32Array(S), total: Int32Array(S)} and uses cellPieceCount as the only piece-count function.
- In useProject, rebuild it with useMemo keyed on [computed, sections, version]. Any compute, load, kind change, free-piece change or color edit therefore rebuilds it from data. It is never patched for those changes.
- Route every progress-only mutation through one function, applyProgressChange(index, data, idx, before, after). It adds popcount(after & m) - popcount(before & m) to placed[sec], where m = (1 << cellPieceCount) - 1. This covers togglePiecePlaced (StepPlan.tsx:100, StoneDialog.tsx:161) and setCellPlaced without assuming which direction the change goes.
- For setRangePlaced (StepPlan.tsx:210, 220), recount only that section.
- The progress useMemo (useProject.ts:222-228) reads placed[] and total[], with overall totals = sum over sections.
- total[] never changes on progress-only operations.

4) Tests in tests/progressIndex.test.ts, plus a dev-only assert:
- Run random sequences of toggle, setCellPlaced, setRangePlaced, setCellKind, setFreePieces and setPieceColor, rebuilding the index on every version change.
- After each step, assert per-section placed and total equal progressOf(range).
- Assert the sum of total[] equals computeStats().pieces.
- Assert the selected-section per-color placed sum equals progressOf(section).placed.
- Align the edge cases (pieceCountFast default branch; cellPieces for LINE without params) so all three counts agree.

5) Scope honestly. This removes about 50-90 ms of main-thread work per tap at 1.4M-3.1M positions and removes the worker backlog. It does NOT fix tap latency at typical sizes on phones. At about 60k positions with 4x CPU, progressOf is about 4 ms of about 100 ms per tap, and the rest is the redraw and render pipeline. Track that as a separate, separately profiled finding.

findings.title: A single stone edit rebuilds the whole overview, clones the whole mosaic twice and takes 2.9 s (2M) or 6.4 s (5M) before the counts update
findings.problem: After one color change, touchMosaic bumps version. That (a) rebuilds the overview bitmap for all cells: the Viewer useMemo calls buildOverviewRGBA, creates a new canvas and runs putImageData (Viewer.tsx:44 to 53). (b) It reruns progressOf over all cells and sections. (c) It structured-clones the whole packed mosaic into the stats worker (useProject.ts:253) and recomputes all stats. (d) After 1.2 s it writes the whole mosaic to IndexedDB again (useProject.ts:166), and the structured clone inside put() runs synchronously on the main thread.
findings.evidence: Browser 2M: edit to stats result 2,854 ms, stats worker 2,524 ms, main-thread postMessage clone 28.2 ms, one long task of 63 ms, IDB put of 'mosaics' 44.4 ms synchronous and 85 ms in total (browser/b2m/result.json). Browser 5M: edit to stats result 6,364 ms, worker 5,932 ms, postMessage 47.9 ms, long task 157 ms, IDB 'mosaics' put 35.5 ms synchronous and 76 ms in total (browser/b5m/result.json). Main-thread profile of the 2M edit (browser-prof-edit.cjs, browser/profedit2m/edit.cpuprofile): br = buildOverviewRGBA 26 ms self plus putImageData 5 ms, progressOf about 23 ms, stats onmessage deserialization 15 ms. Node: overview build 33 to 42 ms at 2M and 80 to 93 ms at 5M; packed mosaic 15.3 MB at 2M and 38.2 MB at 5M (res-2m-*.txt, res-5m-*.txt). All paths are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/performance-scale/.
findings.proposal: Make edits incremental from start to finish. (1) Keep the overview RGBA buffer and canvas. On an edit, recompute that cell's pixel and call putImageData with a 1x1 dirty rectangle instead of rebuilding. (2) Keep the mosaic in the stats worker and post diffs such as {idx, kind, c1, c2, sub, line}. The worker subtracts the old pieces' contributions and adds the new ones using the integer-keyed CutInfo cache from the stats finding (under 1 ms), then returns only the changed per-color and per-section rows. (3) Store the mosaic in IndexedDB in row bands (for example 256 rows per key) and write only dirty bands, or do the writes from the worker so cloning stays off the UI thread. The progress store can use the same band approach.
corrected:
Ordered by value. Keep correctness first (req. 9 and 18).

0. Quick win (S): stop the stats queue from piling up. In the stats effect (useProject.ts:246-259), call cancelChannel('stats') before runWorker('stats', ...). This terminates a job that is still running but outdated. Ignore the 'abgebrochen' rejection in the catch block; it currently goes to console.error. Also show statsBusy in the UI: dim the legend and material counts and add a small "wird aktualisiert…" badge in StepPreview, StepColors and the material step, so stale numbers are never shown as final.

1. Incremental stats (M):
- Factor the post-loop part of computeStats into finalizeStats(acc, layout, range, opts). That covers raw/rawWithReserve ceil, packs, cost, finishedArea, jointArea, grout and waste.
- Option a: keep the unpacked mosaic and a CutCache in the stats worker. Send the full mosaic once after compute or load, then send only cell diffs: {idx, kind, c1, c2, sub, line, free}.
- Option b: do it on the main thread. Edits mutate data in place before onChanged() is called, so add an api.beginEdit(row, col) call before setPieceColor, setCellKind or setFreePieces in StoneDialog and StepColors to snapshot the "before" state. Then call touchMosaic([{row, col}]).
- Either way, take the cell's contribution as computeStats(layout, data, palette, materials, opts, {r0: row, r1: row+1, c0: col, c1: col+1}, cache) before and after the edit. Subtract the old, add the new to the total and to the section that contains the cell. This covers pieces, area, rawExact, cut/uncut, placed, perShape, notFitting and the perSize map; drop a key when its count reaches 0. Then re-finalize only the touched rows.
- Prototyped at about 0.03 ms per edit, identical to a full recompute after 200 random edits.
- Do the same for progress toggles: progressVersion currently also triggers a full stats run (useProject.ts:272). They only need placed ±1 on the color, the section and the total.
- Keep one full recompute as a consistency check after 5 s of idle (cancellable as in 0.). If it ever disagrees, replace the incremental result with it.
- Add a vitest that checks incremental == full after random color and kind edits.

2. Incremental overview and progress (S-M):
- Move the per-cell pixel logic out of buildOverviewRGBA into overviewPixel(layout, data, rgb, idx, out).
- In Viewer, keep the RGBA buffer and canvas in refs. Pass dirty cell indices together with version, for example an edit log ref in useProject. On a dirty-only bump, recompute those pixels and call putImageData(img, 0, 0, col, row, 1, 1). Rebuild fully only when layout, data or palette identity changes.
- In the progress memo, keep totals in a ref. For each dirty cell, apply the difference in pieceCountFast and popcount before vs after, instead of re-running progressOf over all cells and 578 sections.

3. Optional, lower priority: storage.
- First remove the redundant saveProgress in touchMosaic's debounced save when only colors changed.
- Only if the profile still shows it: store the mosaic in row bands, all written in a single IDB transaction with a format version field and a migration from the current single record. Or move the IDB write into a worker so the structured clone stays off the UI thread.
- Do not ship banding without a load/save round-trip test, because a partial or inconsistent band layout would mean data loss.

Do these in this order. Each step is safe on its own.

1. (S) Stop the stats queue in useProject.ts:240-272. Before posting a new 'stats' request, cancel the one still running with cancelChannel('stats') and let the worker respawn. Or post only the latest request: if a request is in flight, set a dirty flag and post once more when it returns. Evidence: 5 edits about 1.1 s apart at 2M gave 5 back-to-back full runs and the final counts arrived 8.5 s after the last edit (burst-1000x500-4-5x1000.json).

2. (S) Show statsBusy, which is already returned but never used. Display a small "wird aktualisiert…" or spinner next to the per-colour counts (StepPreview.tsx:87), the palette editor counts (StepColors), the material summary (StepPlan.tsx:300) and the section legends. Stale totals should never look current (requirement 18).

3. (M) Make the full recompute fast instead of incremental. Replace the total-plus-each-section passes (compute.worker.ts:61-62) with one pass that fills per-section x per-colour accumulators, using integer geometry keys (classes of colW and rowH, as in fast-stats-proto.ts: 2M cells, 4720 ms down to 201 ms, 0 mismatches). Sections partition the grid (layout.ts:320-338), so the total is the merge of the sections. To make the result exact regardless of summation order:
   - rawExact: keep integer counts per (colour, yieldPerRaw). yieldPerRaw is an integer (pieces.ts:262-269). Compute the sum of count/yield at the end.
   - area: keep counts per (colour, geometry class) and multiply by the class area. FREE cells are summed separately.
   - perSize: sort by count descending, then by key, so the order is the same everywhere.
   Use the same function in the PDF and CSV workers so the UI, PDF and CSV numbers are identical. Keep the current computeStats as the reference in a vitest test that checks equality on the 4 sample projects and after random setPieceColor, setCellKind, setFreePieces and setRangePlaced edits.

4. (S) Update the overview incrementally. Move the per-cell code of buildOverviewRGBA (render.ts:93-131) into an exported overviewPixel(layout, data, rgb, idx, out) and use it in both the full build and the update. The Viewer keeps the RGBA buffer and canvas in refs. touchMosaic(dirty?: number[]) passes the edited cell indices, and for those the Viewer runs putImageData(img, 0, 0, col, row, 1, 1). If there is no dirty list (palette removal or remap, replaceColor, recompute), or if the palette or layout changed, it rebuilds fully as it does now.

5. (S) Keep progress counters. Maintain Int32Array placed[] and total[] per section, updated inside togglePiecePlaced and setCellPlaced. These are integer and exact. Recount fully on load, after setRangePlaced and setCellKind, and when the section settings change. This removes the progressOf scan over all cells, which costs about 23 ms per tap at 2M and 54 to 82 ms at 5M.

6. Defer the rest, and keep the storage format.
   - Add a worker that keeps the mosaic and receives diffs only if the 5M case is still above about 1 s after steps 1 to 5. If it is built, the main thread sends {baseVersion, dirtyCells}, and the worker answers 'need-full' whenever its base version does not match (after a restart or cancel). A full recompute at idle time then confirms and replaces the result built from diffs.
   - Do not switch IndexedDB to row bands. At most, start the debounced saveMosaic from requestIdleCallback.

findings.title: Laying mode has no row/column orientation and no bulk marking; progress is only per tap or whole section
findings.problem: While laying, the user has to find 'row AI, column 34' on the screen, but the viewer draws only section labels and colour codes, with no row letters, column numbers or ruler. In Verlegemodus, dragging pans instead of marking, so a 40×50 cm portrait (5,969 stones) needs thousands of taps unless a whole 30×30 cm section is marked at once. 'Meine Projekte' does not show laying progress.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-desktop/journey6.out: 'placed after 6 clicks: 6 | after drag across ~11 stones: 6', 'canvas cursor in lay mode: grab'. Screenshot shots/j6-01-laymode.png (no row/col labels). src/core/render.ts only calls fillText for section ids (l.274) and colour codes (l.312). Project list shows only 'berechnet', no %: shots/j3-14-projects.png, src/ui/Projects.tsx:57-59.
findings.proposal: 1) In Viewer.tsx, add sticky top/left gutter overlays (spreadsheet-style) that print column numbers and row letters from layout.colX/rowY for the visible range, shown once stones are at least about 12 px. Add a matching 'Gehe zu' field in the plan step. 2) Lay mode: pointer-drag paints 'verlegt' on every touched piece (Space or two fingers to pan); Shift-drag a rectangle uses the existing setRangePlaced(). Add 'Reihe bis hier verlegt' and 'nächster offener Stein' buttons. 3) Make laid stones clearly visible (desaturated plus check mark). 4) Show '% verlegt' and a mini progress bar per project in Projects.tsx and the home recent cards; progressOf() already exists.
corrected:
1) Row and column labels on screen. In Viewer.tsx, add a thin top and left gutter (about 18 px), drawn in renderMosaic after the cells or as a separate overlay canvas. Use visibleRange(layout, view) to get the visible rows and columns. Print rowLabel(row) at rowY[row]+rowH[row]/2 and col+1 at colX[col]+colW[col]/2, with the same label-skipping rule the PDF uses (labelStep in pdf.ts:605, applied to pitchPx): every label when pitch is at least 14 px, every 5th or 10th when smaller, none in overview mode. This keeps the screen and PDF labels identical. Also highlight the row and column of the selected stone in the gutter.

2) 'Find stone' in the plan step. Move the parseCellId form from StepPreview.tsx:62-77 into a shared component and use it in StepPlan as well. It should centre the stone and highlight it, and in laying mode it should not toggle it.

3) Bulk marking as an explicit choice. Add a Segmented control next to the 'Verlegemodus' toggle with three options: Tippen (current behaviour), Pinsel (paint) and Rechteck (rectangle).
- Pinsel: a one-pointer drag sets laid=true on every piece it touches, or laid=false if the first piece touched was already laid. Use setCellPlaced or a per-piece set, not a toggle, so going over a stone twice does not undo it.
- Rechteck: a drag draws a rectangle, then calls setRangePlaced(layout, data, {r0,r1,c0,c1}, true) for the cells it covers.
- In both modes, two fingers (touch) or Space / middle button (desktop) pan the view, and the cursor changes to crosshair.
- Keep one step of undo: snapshot data.progress before each stroke and show an 'Rückgängig' button.
- In StoneDialog, add 'Reihe in diesem Abschnitt verlegt' and 'Spalte in diesem Abschnitt verlegt'. Use setRangePlaced with {r0:row,r1:row+1,c0:sec.c0,c1:sec.c1} (and the matching column range).
- Add a 'Nächster offener Stein' button: scan data.progress from the start of the selected section, then centre and highlight the first piece that is not laid.

4) Progress in Meine Projekte and on Home. Do not call progressOf() in the list. In useProject.touchProgress and the compute save, write meta.progressPlaced and meta.progressTotal from the progress memo that already exists (useProject.ts:224) and save the record with saveProject. Projects.tsx and the Home cards then show 'NN % verlegt' and a small ProgressBar from these two numbers. If the fields are missing (older projects), show nothing until the project is next opened.

Leave out the original sub-proposal on making laid stones visible: drawPlaced in render.ts already does this. At most, make the check mark appear from 6 px instead of 10 px.

1) Rulers on screen (S-M). Add a 'rulers' option to RenderOptions in src/core/render.ts and turn it on in StepPlan/StepPreview.
- Draw a top band and a left band of about 18 px.
- Put column numbers (col+1) at layout.colX[col]+colW/2 and row labels from rowLabel(row) at rowY+rowH/2, only for the visibleRange.
- When the pitch is under about 14 px, label only every 5th or 10th index so labels do not overlap.
- Use exactly the same labels as cellId() and pdf.ts:617.
- On desktop, add a small status line under the viewer: the hovered stone's pieceId plus X/Y in mm from the existing origin. Compute it with the same indexAt and pointInPolygon logic as onUp.
- Move the existing 'find stone' field (parseCellId, StepPreview.tsx:66-73) into a shared component. Use it in StepPlan too, so it centres and highlights the stone.

2) Faster marking (M). Under the Verlegemodus toggle, add a mode switch: Tippen | Malen | Rechteck.
- In Malen, one-finger or mouse drag sets every piece it touches to the state opposite to the first touched piece. Two fingers (or Space/middle mouse) pan and zoom.
- In Rechteck, drag a cell-snapped rectangle, show 'N Steine als verlegt markieren?', then call setRangePlaced().
- Snapshot data.progress (a Uint16Array copy) before each gesture and add a 'Rückgängig' button with a short history of 10-20 steps.
- During a gesture, call only draw(). Call api.touchProgress() once on pointerup so progressOf over all sections does not run on every move.
- Add 'Nächster offener Stein': in the selected section, or globally, row-major, find the first piece whose progress bit is 0, then centre and highlight it with its ID.
- Drop 'Reihe bis hier verlegt' for now because what it should do is unclear.

3) Visibility of laid stones (S). Keep the existing tick (it already works). Replace the white wash with a desaturating grey or green tint, which also shows on white or light stones. In the overview path (pitch under 3 px), draw a second 1-pixel-per-cell progress overlay so progress is visible on large projects when the whole mosaic is shown.

4) Progress in the project list (S). Do not load mosaics in Projects.tsx. Add an optional field to ProjectMeta: progressSummary {placed, total}.
- Update it wherever progress is saved (the touchProgress save callback and the save after compute in useProject.ts) using progressOf(), and save it with the project.
- Clear it on recompute.
- In Projects.tsx and the Home recent cards, show 'x % verlegt' with a mini ProgressBar only when the field exists. Otherwise show nothing rather than an estimate.

findings.title: Recompute silently wipes laying progress and all manual stone edits, with no confirmation and no backup
findings.problem: Clicking 'Neu berechnen' replaces MosaicData, including the progress bitmask and every manual colour or shape edit, and saves the new zero progress straight away. Requirement 14 says progress must be persisted, and requirement 13 depends on manual edits being kept. There is no confirm dialog, no snapshot and no undo. The only safeguard is a grey sentence below the button. The 'stale' badge also keeps prompting the user to recompute after any setting change.
findings.evidence: Reproduction /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/spec-gaps/b2.cjs. Steps: open the portrait sample, mark section A1 done, recompute. Output: 'placed before recompute: 1.526 (25,6 %); after recompute: 0 (0 %); confirm dialogs shown: 0 []'. Code: src/ui/project/useProject.ts:320 unpacks the fresh result, and useProject.ts:346 saves it, including the zeroed progress, with saveProgress(id, progress). StepCompute.tsx calls api.compute() directly from the button. The only safeguard is the passive text 'compute.overwriteWarn' (src/i18n/de.ts:229).
findings.proposal: 1) Guard: in StepCompute, when progressOf(...).placed > 0 or edits exist, open a modal that states exact counts ('1.526 verlegte Steine, 37 manuell geänderte Steine gehen verloren'). Offer 'Sicherung anlegen und neu berechnen' or 'Abbrechen'. 2) Versions: add an IndexedDB store 'versions' {projectId, ts, record, mosaic, progress} in src/storage/db.ts, reusing the exportProject serialisation from projects.ts. Write a version automatically before every recompute, and list and restore versions in Projects. 3) Exact carry-over, with no guessing: keep the old data until the new data is ready. For each cell where cellGeomKey (stats.ts) is unchanged and every piece has the same palette HEX, copy the progress bits. Leave all other cells unplaced and report 'N verlegte Steine haben sich geändert – bitte prüfen'. 4) Add an 'edited' Uint8 mask that setPieceColor, setCellKind and setFreePieces set. findings.title: Small but essential colours disappear from the palette: no black for pupils, weak lip and highlight colours
findings.problem: k-means (kmeans.ts, sample weights from mosaic.ts:425-440) minimises area-weighted squared error. Tiny but crucial features — pupils, catchlights, the darkest lip line — are merged into large clusters, even with face weight 3. Eyes are the most important part of a portrait, and they lose their pupils.
findings.evidence: Script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/algo-quality/exp-misc.ts (output .../out/results/exp-misc.txt, check 'portrait-small-features'), on the bundled portrait sample with its face region and 32 colours. Pupil (L* = 3): nearest palette colour is #321D12, ΔE00 14.1, so there is no black in the palette. Catchlight 5.6, lips 7.5; large skin areas 0.7–0.9. Visual: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/algo-quality/out/portrait-face-cmp.png (irises without pupils or highlights; the left iris becomes a diagonal-triangle 'arrow'). A crude prototype, 'reserve 3 colours' in .../algo-quality/exp-proto.ts (k−3 k-means plus 3 farthest-point colours supported by at least 2 cells), lowers the pupil ΔE from 14.1 to 8.3 at +0.05 global perceived ΔE. On the astronaut photo it raises face p95 by 0.3, so a proper objective is needed rather than a bolt-on.
findings.proposal: Weight palette samples by importance: w = area · (1 + 2·det) · faceWeight. After Lloyd, run an error-driven swap: repeatedly try replacing the palette colour with the smallest marginal loss by the weighted mean of the worst-represented cluster (samples with ΔE00 > 10). Keep the swap only if total weighted ΔE00 (not squared) decreases. Seed near-black and near-white automatically when at least 0.2 % of samples have L* < 15 or > 95. Add a regression test: portrait-sample pupil ΔE < 6 while the global mean rises by no more than 0.05.
corrected:
Add a post-Lloyd palette refinement in src/core/kmeans.ts, e.g. refinePalette(pts, w, centers, opts), and call it from mosaic.ts after kmeansLab for paletteMode 'auto' and 'auto-snap'.

1. Assign every sample with ΔE00, the same metric NearestColorMatcher uses. For each sample keep the best distance d1, the second-best d2 and the assigned centre a1.

2. Build candidate groups, in this order:
   - (a) Dark extremes: samples with L* < 15 and d1 > 6.
   - (b) Light extremes: samples with L* > 92 and d1 > 6.
   - (c) General outliers: cluster the samples with d1 > 10 into up to 4 groups with a small k-means.
   Each group needs at least 3 stones, counted by number, not by weight. The candidate colour is the group's weighted mean.

3. For each candidate:
   - Compute each palette colour's marginal loss as Σ w·(d2 − d1) over its members, and replace the colour with the smallest loss.
   - Accept the swap if the weighted mean ΔE00 (L1, not squared) rises by at most 0.05 for an extreme group (a or b), or does not rise at all for a general group (c).
   - Do NOT stop at the first rejected candidate. Allow at most about 4 accepted swaps.
   - Freeze accepted centres so further Lloyd steps cannot pull them back into the hair-brown cluster.
   - Re-evaluate only the members of the replaced colour plus the candidate group, so this stays fast at k = 200.

4. In auto-snap mode the rescued centre then snaps to the nearest material, so a black tile is used if one is in stock.

5. Add a vitest, e.g. tests/palette-extremes.test.ts:
   - On the bundled portrait with the face ellipse (0.27/0.25/0.46/0.5) at 32 colours, the stones covering the pupil pixels near (337,440) have ΔE00 < 6, and the overall weighted mean ΔE00 is at most 0.05 above the current baseline.

6. Optional, cheap UI help in StepColors PaletteEditor: when a colour is added after computing, offer 'assign closer stones' (assign this colour to every stone whose ΔE to it is lower than to its current colour). Totals update as usual, so the user can add black for the pupils in one step instead of clicking every stone.

7. Drop or separately benchmark the untested (1+2·det) weight change.

Impact 3 for portraits whose photo has no large dark area elsewhere; otherwise it changes little. Effort M.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
